batch_notes: Gated generators without a cited id are common: several properties narrow their inputs to exactly the shapes that work (go/now whole-minute fixed offsets for now/1 and 3/6/9-digit fractions for now/7 and timeOnly-then-date order for now/10; pflag ASCII-only usage text for pflag/5; termenv genRGBHex(ht, true) for termenv/2, COLORFGBG 0-15 for termenv/5, four-digit replies for termenv/7; reflow chunks that never split a rune for reflow/15). I attributed these as inferred, but they are a distinct shape between explicit and inferred (generator gate, no id) the rubric might want to name. go/timefmt-go has two 'properties' that are fixed tables of 4-6 cases drawn at random inside property() (TestHegelMinusFlagWithSmallWidthDoesNotPad, TestHegelOrdinalDayWinsOverPartialDates); they carry bugs_direct and I tagged them pin, but they are really example tests and will inflate property bug rates unless pins are excluded. A recurring shape the rubric places awkwardly: expected values built from stdlib primitives inside the test (go/now clock units via time.Date, shellescape filterRunes over unicode.IsPrint, termenv's computed xterm palette) - I filed these as model-oracle since the stdlib is a building block, not an independent implementation. Round-trips through external tools (shellescape through bash/dash/ash) and oracles reached through child processes (Perl, glibc via Python ctypes, Python shlex) are well represented in this batch. Data quality: go/termenv properties have empty comment and readme fields (the README documents them in a table the extractor did not parse), and every readme_head is truncated at about 3500 characters, so README attribution hints beyond the first few properties are unavailable; bodies are cut at ~45 lines, which hid the tail of several properties (termenv Output, pflag TypedValues). reflow/6 is in bugs_direct of two properties and regexp2/1 of four; I named one property per bug.
